hot_topics.topic: Matrix-aware / spectral optimizers (Muon and successors)
hot_topics.why_now: Newton-Schulz orthogonalization made an approximately second-order weight update cheap enough per step to survive frontier-scale pretraining, so AdamW stopped being the automatic default for the first time in roughly eight years. The practice ran ahead of the theory, and 2026 is the year the theory is catching up.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: ICML 2026 workshop 'High Dimensional Learning Dynamics: the Science of Scaling' (the HiLD series, whose ICML 2025 edition was titled '3rd Workshop on High-dimensional Learning Dynamics'); NeurIPS 2025 workshop 'OPT 2025: Optimization for Machine Learning'; NeurIPS 2025 workshop 'Dynamics at the Frontiers of Optimization, Sampling, and Games'. arXiv cs.LG carried ~25 Muon-specific papers in June-July 2026 alone, e.g. 'Towards Understanding the Power and Limits of the Muon Optimizer: A River-Valley Perspective' (2026-06-19), 'SOAP, Muon, and Beyond: Pushing LLM Pretraining Scales' (2026-07-13), 'An Isotropy-Preserving Spectral Cap for Muon' (2026-07-22).
hot_topics.one_line: Instead of scaling each weight independently like Adam does, these optimizers treat a weight matrix as a single geometric object and normalize the whole update's shape, which trains large models faster for the same compute.

hot_topics.topic: The science of scaling: learning dynamics replacing loss-curve extrapolation
hot_topics.why_now: Chinchilla-style compute-vs-loss curves stopped predicting the things people now buy models for (reasoning, post-training gains, low-precision behavior). Cheap small-scale replication rigs and open training traces made it affordable to study the trajectory rather than only the endpoint.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: ICML 2026 workshop 'High Dimensional Learning Dynamics: the Science of Scaling' (note the explicit rename toward scaling from the ICML 2025 'HiLD' title); ICLR 2026 workshop 'Scientific Methods for Understanding Deep Learning (Sci4DL)'; ICML 2025 workshop 'Methods and Opportunities at Small Scale (MOSS)'; NeurIPS 2025 workshop 'Evaluating the Evolving LLM Lifecycle: Benchmarks, Emergent Abilities, and Scaling'.
hot_topics.one_line: Rather than fitting a curve that says a bigger model will score better, researchers now study how the model changes during training so they can predict which capabilities appear and when.

hot_topics.topic: Causal auditing of sparse-autoencoder features (interpretability's replication turn)
hot_topics.why_now: Sparse autoencoders became cheap and standard across 2024-2025, so by 2026 the open question flipped from 'can we extract interpretable features' to 'do those features actually cause the behavior, or are they decorative'. A visible cluster of falsification and audit papers is the result.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: NeurIPS 2025 'Workshop on Mechanistic Interpretability' and ICML 2026 'Workshop on Mechanistic Interpretability' (a repeat main-cycle workshop, i.e. the parent field is mainstream); ICML 2025 workshop 'Actionable Interpretability'; NeurIPS 2025 'CogInterp: Interpreting Cognition in Deep Learning Models'. The audit turn itself is visible on arXiv in July 2026: 'Are Single-Token Sparse Autoencoder Features Causally Necessary?' (2026-07-22), 'From Geometric Recovery to Causal Validation: A Reproducible Audit of Sparse Autoencoder Features' (2026-07-13), 'When Are Sparse Feature Interventions Actually Localized?' (2026-07-11), 'The Model Organism Lottery' (2026-07-01).
hot_topics.one_line: Interpretability tools claim to find human-readable concepts inside a network, and the current wave of work tests whether editing those concepts actually changes the model's behavior instead of just looking meaningful.

hot_topics.topic: Uncertainty quantification for agentic and multi-step systems
hot_topics.why_now: Conformal prediction is now a solved, packaged tool for single predictions, but agents chain dozens of model calls and a per-call coverage guarantee says almost nothing about whether the whole trajectory is right. Retargeting the existing statistical machinery at pipelines is the open problem.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: ICML 2026 workshop 'Statistical Frameworks for Uncertainty in Agentic Systems' (first edition, no ordinal in title); ICML 2026 'The 2nd Workshop on Epistemic Intelligence in Machine Learning'; NeurIPS 2025 'ML x OR: Mathematical Foundations and Operational Integration of Machine Learning for Uncertainty-Aware Decision-Making'. For contrast, plain conformal prediction is unambiguously mainstream: an arXiv scan of the last four weeks returned 40+ conformal papers that are almost entirely domain applications (motorsport powertrains, sepsis transcriptomics, radiomics, motion planning), which is the application-saturation signature of a settled method.
hot_topics.one_line: Conformal prediction can wrap a single model output in an error bar with a mathematical coverage guarantee, and the new work asks how to keep that guarantee when an agent strings twenty such outputs together.
hot_topics.critic_note: Venue evidence is real: icml.cc/virtual/2026/events/workshop lists 'Statistical Frameworks for Uncertainty in Agentic Systems' (#37) and 'The 2nd Workshop on Epistemic Intelligence in Machine Learning' (#7), verbatim, and the first has no ordinal. Overstated on the survey rule: arXiv 2602.05073 'Uncertainty Quantification in LLM Agents: Foundations, Emerging Challenges, and Opportunities' (2026-02-04) is a survey on exactly this topic, five months before the claimed forming window, and 2503.15850 'Uncertainty Quantification and Confidence Calibration in Large Language Models: A Survey' (2025-03-20, 93 votes) covers the parent. The specific 'open problem' named (per-call coverage does not compose over a pipeline) is already addressed in print: 2605.18812 'PASC: Pipeline-Aware Conformal Prediction with Joint Coverage Guarantees for Multi-Stage NLP and LLM Pipelines' (2026-05-12), plus 2604.22985 UQ for LLM function-calling and 2606.25760 UQ for computer-use agents. This is the weakest of my overstated calls: the venue framing is honest and the sub-area is roughly a year old, not three. Not checked: the NeurIPS 2025 ML x OR workshop.

hot_topics.topic: Latent and implicit reasoning: deliberation in hidden states rather than tokens
hot_topics.why_now: RLVR-trained models made long chains of thought standard, and long chains are expensive in both latency and serving cost. Once test-time compute became the main capability lever, compressing deliberation into recurrent depth or continuous latents became worth the training complexity.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: ICLR 2026 workshop 'Latent & Implicit Thinking - Going Beyond CoT Reasoning' (first edition); NeurIPS 2025 'The First Workshop on Efficient Reasoning'; NeurIPS 2025 'Foundations of Reasoning in Language Models'; ICLR 2026 'From Human Cognition to AI Reasoning'. Representative recent arXiv: 'Training Continuous Chain of Thought Models: A Tale of Two Regimes' (2026-07-18), 'Bridging the Gap Between Latent and Explicit Reasoning with Looped Transformers' (2026-06-30).
hot_topics.one_line: Instead of making a model write out its reasoning as text it can be made to loop internally and think in its own hidden representation, which is cheaper but much harder to inspect.
hot_topics.critic_note: Decisively overstated. Two direct surveys predate the claimed forming window by about a year: arXiv 2507.06203 'A Survey on Latent Reasoning' (2025-07-08, 217 votes) and 2509.02350 'Implicit Reasoning in Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey' (2025-09-02, 150 votes). A third synthesis, 2604.02029 'The Latent Space: Foundation, Evolution, Mechanism, Ability, and Outlook' (2026-04-02, 258 votes), is already an outlook paper. The line is also high-attention mainstream, not pre-mainstream: 2510.25741 'Scaling Latent Reasoning via Looped Language Models' has 345 votes and 7789 views, and there is a position paper (2604.15726 'LLM Reasoning Is Latent, Not the Chain of Thought') arguing the framing should be the field default. The two arXiv exemplars cited are real and correctly dated (2607.16972 on 2026-07-18; 2606.31779 Looped Transformers on 2026-06-30, the claim's '2607' prefix for the latter is wrong but the date is right). Workshop titles being first editions does not rescue a topic with two comprehensive surveys already published.

hot_topics.topic: Diffusion and masked-discrete language models as an alternative to autoregression
hot_topics.why_now: Parallel token decoding stopped being a research toy once serving stacks, KV-cache adaptations, and RL post-training recipes for diffusion LMs appeared. The bottleneck moved from 'does this generate coherent text' to 'does it beat autoregression on tokens-per-second at equal quality'.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: ICML 2026 workshop 'Foundations of Deep Generative Models: Understanding Memorization, Generalization, and Reasoning'; ICLR 2026 'Deep Generative Model in Machine Learning: Theory, Principle and Efficacy (2nd Workshop)'; NeurIPS 2025 'Structured Probabilistic Inference and Generative Modeling' and ICML 2026 '4th Structured Probabilistic Inference & Generative Modeling'. The systems turn is visible on arXiv: 'Sangam: Efficiently Serving Diffusion LLMs with the AR Stack' (2026-07-05), 'DiLaServe: High SLO Attainment Serving for Diffusion Language Models' (2026-06-27), 'Nemotron-Labs-TwoTower' (2026-06-25).
hot_topics.one_line: Normal language models write one token at a time left to right, while diffusion language models start from a masked or noisy sequence and refine many positions in parallel, trading a harder training recipe for lower latency.

hot_topics.topic: Weight-space learning and neural network symmetries (principled model merging)
hot_topics.why_now: There are now millions of public fine-tuned checkpoints of a handful of base models, which turns the weight space itself into a dataset. What blocks naive averaging is that permuting neurons or rescaling layers leaves a network's function unchanged, so two good checkpoints can sit in incompatible coordinates.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: ICML 2026 'Workshop on Weight-Space Symmetries: from Foundations to Practical Applications' (first edition); ICML 2026 'The 2nd Workshop on Connecting Low-rank Representations in AI: From Practice to Theory'; NeurIPS 2025 'UniReps: Unifying Representations in Neural Models'; ICLR 2026 'Representational Alignment'.
hot_topics.one_line: Two independently trained networks can compute the same thing while storing it in shuffled or rescaled weights, so merging or comparing models requires first undoing those hidden symmetries.
hot_topics.critic_note: Decisively overstated on three independent grounds. First, the 'first edition' framing is misleading: ICLR 2025 already ran a weight-space workshop, 'Neural Network Weights as a New Data Modality' (confirmed on iclr.cc/virtual/2025/events/workshop), so only the ICML 2026 title is new, not the venue track. The claim's own corroborator undercuts it too: ICLR 2025 already hosted the 'Second Workshop on Representational Alignment (Re2-Align)', making the cited ICLR 2026 edition at least the third. Second, surveys exist: 2603.10090 'A Survey of Weight Space Learning: Understanding, Representation, and Generation' (2026-03-10), 2603.09938 'Model Merging in the Era of Large Language Models' (2026-03-10), 2410.12927 'Deep Model Merging: The Sister of Neural Network Interpretability, A Survey' (2024-10-16), plus an entire thesis, 2605.01580 'Model Merging: Foundations and Algorithms' (2026-05-02). Third, well past three years hot: Git Re-Basin (2209.04836) is from 2022, with permutation-symmetry and mode-connectivity work older still. The ICML 2026 workshop title itself is confirmed verbatim (#20).

hot_topics.topic: Expressivity limits of transformers: what the architecture provably cannot do
hot_topics.why_now: Circuit-complexity characterizations of fixed-depth attention matured enough to give hard negative results, and chain-of-thought plus recurrence became the concrete, studied escape hatch from those limits, which turns an abstract theory question into an architecture-selection question.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: NeurIPS 2025 workshop "What Can('t) Transformers Do?"; ICML 2026 workshop 'Combining Theory and Benchmarks: Towards A Virtuous Cycle to Understand and Guarantee Foundation Model Performance'; COLT 2026, the 39th Annual Conference on Learning Theory, San Diego, June 29 to July 3 2026 (dates confirmed from learningtheory.org/colt2026); ICLR 2026 'Workshop on Logical Reasoning of Large Language Models'.
hot_topics.one_line: A transformer of fixed depth can only perform a bounded amount of sequential computation per token, so some problems are provably out of reach unless the model is allowed to write intermediate steps or loop.

hot_topics.topic: Memorization as a measurable quantity
hot_topics.why_now: Extraction attacks and capacity-in-bits estimates gave memorization an actual number instead of an intuition, arriving at the same moment that copyright litigation and privacy regulation started demanding one. Measurement got cheap enough to run on production-scale models.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: ICML 2025 'The Impact of Memorization on Trustworthy Foundation Models' followed by ICML 2026 'The Second Workshop on the Impact of Memorization on Trustworthy Foundation Models' (a two-edition series, so incubating rather than forming); ICML 2026 'Foundations of Deep Generative Models: Understanding Memorization, Generalization, and Reasoning'; ICML 2025 'Machine Unlearning for Generative AI'; NeurIPS 2025 'Regulatable ML: Towards Bridging the Gaps between Machine Learning Research and Regulations'.
hot_topics.one_line: Researchers can now estimate roughly how many bits of its training data a model has stored verbatim, which turns 'is it memorizing or generalizing' from a debate into a measurement.

hot_topics.topic: Test-time updates and continual foundation-model maintenance
hot_topics.why_now: Shipping frozen weights collides with real drift, and post-training got cheap enough that updating a deployed model is now routine. The unsolved part is doing it without silently breaking behavior that downstream users already depend on.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: ICLR 2026 'The 3rd Workshop on Test-Time Updates (TTU)', which grew out of ICML 2025 '2nd Workshop on Test-Time Adaptation: Putting Updates to the Test (PUT)'; NeurIPS 2025 'AI That Keeps Up: Workshop on Continual and Compatible Foundation Model Updates (CCFM)' (first edition); ICML 2026 'Continual Adaptation at Scale: Towards Sustainable AI'; ICLR 2026 'Catch, Adapt, and Operate: Monitoring ML Models Under Drift'.
hot_topics.one_line: A deployed model's world keeps changing, so this line of work updates the model after deployment while guaranteeing the update does not quietly break things that used to work.

hot_topics.topic: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials and their disorder frontier
hot_topics.subdomain: computational materials discovery and lab automation
hot_topics.why_now: Pretraining on periodic-table-scale DFT datasets turned ab-initio-accuracy molecular dynamics into a model download rather than a months-long per-system fitting project. The open question therefore moved from 'can we fit one' to 'where does it silently break', and the 2026 benchmark wave answers: amorphous and glassy phases, finite-temperature ensembles, and thermal conductivity.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: AI4Mat-NeurIPS-2025 (AI for Accelerated Materials Design), verified on the neurips.cc 2025 workshop list; same series verified as AI4Mat-2024 at NeurIPS and AI4MAT-ICLR-2025 on iclr.cc. Matbench Discovery leaderboard (matbench-discovery.materialsproject.org), 41 models, last updated 2026-04-07, top entries EquiformerV3+DeNS-OAM and TECE-OAM-RRA-1.0 (2026). Position paper: 'Six Open Questions in Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Foundation Models', arXiv 2606.07327 (2026-06-05). Frontier paper: 'Amorphous materials as a frontier challenge for universal interatomic potentials', arXiv 2607.11384 (2026-07-13).
hot_topics.one_line: A single neural network pretrained on millions of quantum-chemistry calculations can now predict the forces between atoms in almost any material thousands of times faster than solving the physics directly, but it degrades noticeably when the material is glassy or disordered rather than a neat crystal.

hot_topics.topic: Agentic self-driving labs: compressing the experimental validation loop
hot_topics.subdomain: computational materials discovery and lab automation
hot_topics.why_now: Robotic synthesis platforms and LLM agents both got cheap enough to run unattended, so the bottleneck shifted from proposing candidates to physically validating them. The 2026 papers explicitly name wet-lab validation, not ideation, as the thing to compress, which is a different problem statement from the 2023-2024 'AI proposes materials' framing.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: 'Towards Agentic AI for Science' workshop, ICLR 2025, verified on the iclr.cc workshop list; 'AI for Science: Reach and Limits of AI for Scientific Discovery', NeurIPS 2025, verified on neurips.cc (the 'Limits' framing is itself new relative to the 2024 'Foundation Models for Science' workshop). Representative work: 'Compressing the Validation Bottleneck: An Agentic Self-Driving Lab for Scientific Discovery', arXiv 2607.04508 (2026-07-05); 'NIMO: A Software Platform for Closed-Loop Materials Exploration with Diverse AI Algorithms', arXiv 2606.15522 (2026-06-14); 'Rethinking Scientific Discovery in the Agentic Era', arXiv 2607.03863 (2026-07-04).
hot_topics.one_line: Instead of a human choosing the next experiment, an AI agent proposes it, a robot runs it, and the measured result feeds back into the agent, so the physical laboratory rather than the thinking becomes the slow step.

hot_topics.topic: Atomistic language models: LLMs that natively read and write crystal structures
hot_topics.why_now: Earlier attempts either had the language model call an atomistic model as an external tool, or fine-tuned it on lossy text encodings that discarded 3D geometry. Tokenizations that keep coordinates and symmetry intact removed that tradeoff, so one model can now read a structure, reason about it in prose, and emit a new candidate structure in the same forward pass.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: AI4Mat-NeurIPS-2025 scope explicitly covers 'AI-Guided Materials Design' (verified on neurips.cc). Anchor paper: 'Atomistic Language Models Understand and Generate Materials', arXiv 2606.21395 (2026-06-19) - the highest-engagement item in my materials sweep at 28 votes / 268 views on alphaXiv. Adjacent: 'Lang2MLIP: End-to-End Language-to-Machine Learning Interatomic Potential Development with Autonomous Agentic Workflows', arXiv 2605.14527 (2026-05-14); 'Agentic Fusion of Large Atomic and Language Models to Accelerate Superconductor Discovery', arXiv 2604.23758 (2026-04-26). Corroborated by 'Property-Guided Diffusion for Inverse Design of Crystalline Materials' in the arxiv.org/list/cond-mat.mtrl-sci recent batch (181 new entries, 2026-07-24 to 2026-07-27).
hot_topics.one_line: Language models are being taught to read and write the actual 3D atomic coordinates of a crystal, so you can ask for a material in plain English and get back a candidate structure rather than a paragraph describing one.
hot_topics.critic_note: The why_now is contradicted by prior art. 'Language models can generate molecules, materials, and protein binding sites directly in three dimensions' is arXiv 2305.05708 (May 2023), which is precisely the capability the claim says only became possible recently. Earlier still: Crystal Transformer (2204.11953, Apr 2022) and Materials Transformers (2206.13578, Jun 2022); then 'Fine-Tuned Language Models Generate Stable Inorganic Materials as Text' (2402.04379, Feb 2024). Surveys already exist: 'Materials science in the era of large language models: a perspective' (2403.06949, Mar 2024) and 'From Text to Insight: Large Language Models for Materials Science Data Extraction' (2407.16867, Jul 2024), within 104 title matches. AI4Mat is a recurring dedicated venue, not a new one: verified at neurips.cc/virtual/2024, neurips.cc/virtual/2025 and as 'AI4MAT-ICLR-2026' in the iclr.cc/virtual/2026 list. The anchor paper is genuine (2606.21395, Edamadaka et al., 19 Jun 2026); the field around it is not new.

hot_topics.topic: Magic state cultivation and low-overhead fault tolerance
hot_topics.why_now: Cultivation replaced multi-round magic state distillation factories with a single fault-tolerant growth procedure, cutting the space-time overhead of the non-Clifford gates that give quantum computers their power. That changed resource estimates for a useful fault-tolerant machine by roughly an order of magnitude, so the 2026 literature is a rapid design-space search over catalysts, code switching, and factory layouts rather than a debate about feasibility.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: IEEE Quantum Week QCE 2026 (Metro Toronto Convention Centre, 2026-09-13 to 09-18), tracks QALG (Algorithms) and QTEM (Technologies and Engineering) plus 46 workshops, verified on qce.quantum.ieee.org. Quantum (journal) Volume 10, July 2026: error correction and fault tolerance are the dominant recurring theme, verified on quantum-journal.org. Dated cluster: 'Efficient Magic State Cultivation for sqrt(T) Gates', arXiv 2606.10430 (2026-06-09); 'Cultivating logical catalysts for fault-tolerant dyadic phase rotations', arXiv 2606.27358 (2026-06-25); 'Low Spatial Cost CCZ Magic State Factory', arXiv 2606.24170 (2026-06-23); 'A framework for low-overhead quantum fault tolerance via spacetime lifting', arXiv 2606.06365 (2026-06-04).
hot_topics.one_line: Quantum computers need special 'magic states' to perform their hardest operations, and a technique called cultivation grows those states cheaply in place instead of purifying them through many wasteful rounds, which substantially shrinks the machine needed to do useful work.

hot_topics.topic: Contested quantum advantage and the tuned-classical-baseline arms race
hot_topics.why_now: Almost every quantum advantage claim from 2023-2025 was matched or beaten by a better-tuned classical simulation within months. The field's centre of gravity therefore moved from making a claim to designing certification protocols that survive a well-resourced classical adversary, including adversaries holding side information about the benchmark. This is a benchmark-integrity problem, not a hardware problem.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: IEEE QCE 2026 tracks QAPP (Applications) and QML (Machine Learning), verified on qce.quantum.ieee.org; the track list also includes a QGDD 'GenAI and Discovery' track, which is new relative to the classic QCE track set. Dated cluster: 'When Classical Baselines Are Tuned as Carefully as the Quantum Model, Does Quantum Reservoir Computing Still Win?', arXiv 2607.09905 (2026-07-10); 'Pushing the Classical Frontier of 1D Fermi-Hubbard Quench Dynamics Beyond Current Quantum Simulations', arXiv 2606.04771 (2026-06-03, a direct rebuttal of a Q-CTRL hardware result); 'Loophole-Robust Certification of Quantum Advantage', arXiv 2607.13090 (2026-07-13); 'Benchmarking quantum simulation at scale', arXiv 2607.14212 (2026-07-15); 'Quantum-classical crossover in fault-tolerant quantum dynamics simulation', arXiv 2607.16116 (2026-07-17). CAVEAT: I could not verify the QGDD track's founding year because the qce.quantum.ieee.org subpage returned HTTP 404.
hot_topics.one_line: Nearly every announcement that a quantum computer beat all classical computers has later been matched by someone writing a smarter classical program, so the field is now building certification protocols specifically designed to survive that rebuttal.

hot_topics.topic: Altermagnetism as a third magnetic phase
hot_topics.why_now: Altermagnets combine the compensated zero net moment and terahertz dynamics of an antiferromagnet with the spin-split electronic bands of a ferromagnet, via crystal symmetry rather than relativistic spin-orbit coupling. By 2025-2026 the confirmed material list outgrew the original candidates, so the work moved from 'does this class exist' to engineering: finding altermagnetic order coexisting with superconductivity, in kagome lattices, in spin-density-wave states, and in photonic analogues.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: Founding framing paper: L. Smejkal, J. Sinova, T. Jungwirth, 'Emerging Research Landscape of Altermagnetism', Phys. Rev. X 12, 040501 (2022). Current volume: eight distinct altermagnetism papers dated 2026-06-03 to 2026-07-20 surfaced in a single alphaXiv topical sweep, including 'Stripe-Order Altermagnetism' (2607.17997), 'Emergent d-wave altermagnetism in chlorine-adsorbed FeSe monolayer' (2607.15197), 'Berry-Curvature Activation by Orbital Flux in a Kagome Altermagnet' (2606.04984), and 'Mirror-Symmetry-Enforced Photonic Altermagnet' (2606.21545). 'Altermagnetism' also recurs as a named theme in the arxiv.org/list/cond-mat.mtrl-sci recent batch (181 new entries, 2026-07-24 to 07-27). CAVEAT: I could not verify a 2026 APS Global Physics Summit focus session on altermagnetism because aps.org returned HTTP 403 and summit.aps.org returned HTTP 500; my recollection that such focus sessions have run since 2024 is moderate-confidence and unverified here.
hot_topics.one_line: Altermagnets are a third kind of magnet, identified in 2022, that appear non-magnetic from outside because their magnetism cancels, yet internally split electron energies by spin the way an ordinary magnet does, which makes them attractive for fast memory with no stray magnetic field.

hot_topics.topic: Evolving dark energy after DESI DR2
hot_topics.why_now: DESI's baryon acoustic oscillation measurements became precise enough that the dark energy equation of state no longer sits comfortably at the cosmological-constant value w = -1, and the preferred fit crosses the phantom divide. A parameter that went unquestioned for 25 years is now a live empirical target, which has spawned a large industry of beyond-Lambda-CDM model building and a parallel argument about whether the significance is real.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: 'Dark Energy in the DESI Era: A Brief Review of Evidence, Beyond-Lambda-CDM Interpretations, and Tensions', arXiv 2606.21826 (2026-06-20) - the existence of a review is precisely why I call this mainstream rather than emerging. Significance is itself contested: 'Model-Independent Analysis of Type Ia Supernova Datasets and Implications for Dark Energy', arXiv 2604.11883 (2026-04-13) reports that DESI DR2 + CMB + SNe Ia evidence for dynamical dark energy spans 2.8 to 4.2 sigma depending on which supernova sample is used. Bayesian reassessment: 'The Bayesian view of DESI DR2', arXiv 2603.05472 (2026-03-05). Model-building volume: 'Neutrino mass constraints in interacting dark energy models after DESI DR2', arXiv 2606.05005 (2026-06-03); 'Dissipative Dark Energy can explain the DESI phantom crossing', arXiv 2606.04886 (2026-06-03). CAVEAT: desi.lbl.gov returned HTTP 403, so the DESI DR2 release announcement itself is unverified in this session.
hot_topics.one_line: The best current map of cosmic expansion suggests dark energy has been weakening over time, which the standard cosmological constant model forbids, though how strong that evidence is depends heavily on which supernova catalogue you trust.

hot_topics.topic: Thermodynamic and probabilistic-bit computing hardware for AI
hot_topics.subdomain: statistical physics and physics-based computing hardware
hot_topics.why_now: Frontier-model training and inference energy became a hard economic constraint at the same time that CMOS-integrated stochastic magnetic tunnel junctions crossed the million-p-bit scale. Hardware that treats thermal noise as the computational resource rather than as an error to suppress therefore stopped being a thought experiment and became a fabricated, benchmarked device class in 2026.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: 'ML with New Compute Paradigms' (MLNCP) workshop, NeurIPS 2024, scope covering '(opto-)analog, neuromorphic hardware' - verified on the neurips.cc 2024 workshop list. NOTE, and this is a genuine negative signal: MLNCP does NOT appear in the verified neurips.cc 2025 workshop list, so I cannot confirm the series continued; mlwithnewcompute.com failed to fetch with a TLS certificate error. Hardware milestones instead carry the evidence: 'Programmable Probabilistic Computer with 1,000,000 p-bits', arXiv 2606.25313 (2026-06-24); 'Quantum-Driven Neuromorphic Computing for Million-Qubit-Scale Workloads' describing the Apollo 10000-node 16nm mixed-signal processor at ~0.5 W, arXiv 2606.12968 (2026-06-11); 'Scaling Up Thermodynamic AI Models', arXiv 2607.00170 (2026-06-30); 'Experimental Demonstration of an On-Chip CMOS-Integrated 3T-1MTJ Probabilistic Bit', arXiv 2604.05191 (2026-04-06).
hot_topics.one_line: Rather than fighting the random thermal jitter inside a chip, this hardware uses that jitter as the computation, building 'probabilistic bits' that naturally sample from probability distributions and so run certain AI and optimisation workloads at a small fraction of the energy.
hot_topics.critic_note: Two prior surveys settle it: 'Probabilistic computing with p-bits' (Kaiser and Datta, 2108.09836, Aug 2021) and 'A full-stack view of probabilistic computing with p-bits: devices, architectures and algorithms' (2302.06457, Feb 2023). The device line starts at 'Stochastic p-bits for Invertible Logic' (1610.00377, Oct 2016), ten years back, with 31 title matches. The cited hardware papers are real (2604.05191 and 2606.25313 both appear in the arXiv title listing). The venue evidence fails on its own terms and I confirmed both halves independently: 'ML with New Compute Paradigms' is present in the neurips.cc/virtual/2024 workshop list and absent from the neurips.cc/virtual/2025 list, so the sole named venue is a series with no confirmed 2025 or 2026 edition.

hot_topics.topic: Higher-order networks: dynamics on hypergraphs and simplicial complexes
hot_topics.why_now: Datasets that record who was in the room, not merely who talked to whom, became routine (co-authorship, co-purchase, protein complexes, group conversations). The mathematics of synchronisation, contagion and structural collapse under genuinely many-body coupling matured enough by late 2025 to support a consensus review, and the machine-learning side is now arguing about expressivity limits of hypergraph neural networks.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: 'Collective dynamics on higher-order networks', arXiv 2510.05253 (2025-10-06), a multi-institution review authored across Oxford, Santa Fe Institute, Central European University, UCLouvain, Namur, Exeter, Granada, TUM and VU Amsterdam - a review with that author base marks the area mainstream rather than emerging. Ongoing 2026 work: 'Immunization on Temporal Higher-Order Networks', arXiv 2607.10171 (2026-07-11); 'Hypergraph backboning', arXiv 2606.00893 (2026-05-30); 'The WidthWall: A Strict Expressivity Hierarchy for Hypergraph Neural Networks', arXiv 2605.13690 (2026-05-13); 'Topology and higher-order global synchronization on directed and hollow simplicial and cell complexes', arXiv 2602.09715 (2026-02-10, Queen Mary University of London and Namur). CAVEAT: the Journal of Physics Complexity focus-issue index returned HTTP 404, so I could not confirm a named special issue.
hot_topics.one_line: Standard network science assumes interactions happen between pairs of things, but many real systems involve whole groups acting at once, and modelling those group interactions directly changes the predictions for synchronisation, epidemics and structural collapse.

hot_topics.topic: Foundation models and agent benchmarks for collider physics
hot_topics.why_now: LHC Run 3 simulation volume made per-analysis neural network training the dominant computational cost, so particle physics is copying the pretrain-once-finetune-many pattern, including neural scaling laws and cross-domain transfer from jets to neutrino interactions. In parallel, and this is the newer signal, the first benchmarks appeared that test whether an LLM agent can reproduce an entire published physics analysis rather than solve a toy task.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: 'Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences' (ML4PS) workshop, NeurIPS 2024 and NeurIPS 2025, both verified on neurips.cc; scope explicitly spans physics, astronomy, chemistry and materials. A tightly dated cluster all posted 2026-06-12: 'Machine-learned particle flow as a foundation model for collider physics', arXiv 2606.14373; 'JetParticle-JEPA: An Efficient Self-Supervised Representation Learning method for Jet Tagging', arXiv 2606.14813; 'Pre-Training for Simulation-Based Science: A Study on Jet Foundation Model Training Objectives', arXiv 2606.14870. Also 'EveNet: A Foundation Model for Particle Collision Data Analysis', arXiv 2601.17126 (2026-01-23); 'Neural Scaling Laws for Jet Generation', arXiv 2605.28940 (2026-05-27); 'Cross-Domain Transfer with Particle Physics Foundation Models: From Jets to Neutrino Interactions', arXiv 2604.12364 (2026-04-14). Agent-evaluation angle: 'Collider-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents with Particle Physics Analysis Reproduction', arXiv 2605.13950 (2026-05-13).
hot_topics.one_line: Particle physics is moving from training a fresh neural network for every analysis to pretraining one large model on collision data and fine-tuning it, and new benchmarks now test whether an AI agent can reproduce a whole published analysis end to end.

hot_topics.topic: Prediction-powered inference: valid confidence intervals when most of your labels came from a model
hot_topics.why_now: LLMs and modern predictors made pseudo-labels essentially free while gold-standard human labels stayed expensive, so the binding question flipped from 'can we label at scale' to 'how do we get a correct standard error out of a dataset that is 1 percent human-labelled and 99 percent machine-labelled'. The 2023 recipe now has a 2026 theory wave filling in optimality, multi-source pooling, and causal extensions.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: NeurIPS 2024 workshop 'Statistical Frontiers in LLMs and Foundation Models', whose stated scope includes automatic evaluation, model and data auditing, and uncertainty quantification (verified at neurips.cc/virtual/2024/events/workshop). Origin paper: Angelopoulos, Bates, Fannjiang, Jordan, Zrnic, Science 2023. Sustained 2026 output verified via alphaXiv: 'Statistical Optimality of Prediction-Powered Inference' (arXiv 2606.08730, 2026-06-07), 'Multi-Source Prediction-Powered Inference' (2606.21232, 2026-06-19), 'Prediction-Powered Causal Inference by Automatic Debiased Machine Learning and Semi-Supervised Riesz Regression' (2606.12892, 2026-06-11), 'Statistically Reliable LLM-Based Ranking Evaluation via Prediction-Powered Inference' (2606.05308, 2026-06-03).
hot_topics.one_line: If a model labelled most of your data and humans labelled a small slice, prediction-powered inference tells you how to combine the two so your error bars are honest instead of fake-precise.

hot_topics.topic: E-values, testing by betting, and anytime-valid inference
hot_topics.why_now: Dashboards, online experiments, and always-on model monitors are looked at continuously, which silently destroys the guarantee of a fixed-sample p-value. Betting martingales and e-values give a test statistic you may peek at whenever you like and stop whenever you like, and cheap compute made the sequential machinery practical rather than theoretical.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: First-edition 'ICML 2026 Hypothesis Testing Workshop' (verified at icml.cc/virtual/2026/events/workshop), whose description names e-values and applications to model reliability checks and subgroup shift detection. COPA 2025, the Fourteenth Symposium on Conformal and Probabilistic Prediction with Applications, Royal Holloway London, 10 to 12 September 2025, PMLR volume 266, includes 'Testing by Betting for Anomaly Detection', 'Anytime-Valid Tests of Group Invariance through Conformal Prediction', and 'Testing Exchangeability for Multiple Sequences of P-values'. Recent applied work via alphaXiv: 'Anytime-valid testing with e-values and confirmatory adaptive designs' (2606.00878, 2026-05-30), 'Anytime-valid Optimal Policy Identification' (2606.17515, 2026-06-16). Foundational survey: Ramdas, Grunwald, Vovk and Shafer, Statistical Science 2023, which means the core theory is already consolidated.
hot_topics.one_line: Instead of a p-value that is only valid if you fix the sample size in advance, you bet against the null hypothesis and your accumulated winnings are a valid measure of evidence no matter when you stop looking.

hot_topics.topic: Distribution-free uncertainty guarantees for long-horizon agentic systems
hot_topics.why_now: Agents chain many model calls, and a 90 percent coverage guarantee per step does not compose into anything useful over a twenty-step trajectory. This is a genuinely new statistical object, and it appeared as a dedicated workshop for the first time in 2026 rather than as a section of an existing one.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: First-edition ICML 2026 workshop 'Statistical Frameworks for Uncertainty in Agentic Systems' (verified at icml.cc/virtual/2026/events/workshop); its description names 'distribution-free validity layers for coverage, risk, and abstention under heterogeneity and distribution shift', compositional guarantees, and sequential inference for continuous monitoring. Related 2026 preprints via alphaXiv: 'PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents' (2606.08106, 2026-06-06), 'Inference-Time Conformal Reasoning with Valid Factuality Control for Large Language Models' (2606.08831, 2026-06-07), 'Adaptive auditing of AI systems with anytime-valid guarantees' (2605.07002, 2026-05-07).
hot_topics.one_line: Work out how to attach a trustworthy 'I might be wrong, so I abstain' guarantee to an AI agent that takes many steps, given that per-step guarantees do not automatically survive being chained together.

hot_topics.topic: Statistical evaluation of AI systems: treating benchmarks and evals as a measurement problem
hot_topics.subdomain: survey and measurement, applied to AI systems
hot_topics.why_now: Procurement, safety sign-off, and release decisions now rest on leaderboard numbers computed from a few hundred correlated items with no error bars, judged by other models. Statisticians moved in because the failure mode (a 1.2 point benchmark gap that is pure noise) became expensive rather than academic.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: NeurIPS 2024 workshop 'Statistical Frontiers in LLMs and Foundation Models', scope explicitly covering benchmarking, measuring and correcting bias, automatic evaluation, watermarking, model and data auditing, and uncertainty quantification (verified at neurips.cc/virtual/2024). NeurIPS 2025 workshop 'Evaluating the Evolving LLM Lifecycle: Benchmarks, Emergent Abilities, and Scaling' (verified at neurips.cc/virtual/2025). ICML 2026 workshop 'Combining Theory and Benchmarks: Towards A Virtuous Cycle to Understand and Guarantee Foundation Model Performance' (verified at icml.cc/virtual/2026). Method example via alphaXiv: 'CELEUS: Certifiable and Efficient LLM Evaluation via E-Processes' (2606.20820, 2026-06-18).
hot_topics.one_line: A benchmark score is a survey estimate with a sample size and a sampling frame, and this line of work insists you report its uncertainty before claiming one model beat another.

hot_topics.topic: Silicon sampling: LLMs standing in for human survey respondents, and the validity fight around it
hot_topics.why_now: Recruiting human respondents costs money and weeks, while an LLM produces a plausible-looking respondent for fractions of a cent. Social scientists started publishing on simulated samples faster than anyone established when such an estimate is admissible evidence, so 2026 is the year the validity criteria are being written.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: Metascience 2025, University College London, 30 June to 2 July 2025, whose named themes include artificial intelligence and responsible research practices, and where the Metascience Alliance launched (verified at metascience.info/prior-conferences). 2026 preprint wave verified via alphaXiv: 'Silicon Sampling via Cross-Survey Transfer' (2607.03091, 2026-07-03), 'Valid Inference with Synthetic Data via Task Exchangeability' (2606.13629, 2026-06-11), 'This human study did not involve human subjects: Validating LLM simulations as behavioral evidence' (2602.15785, 2026-02-17), 'Validating LLMs in social science: Epistemic threats and emerging norms' (2607.07915, 2026-07-08), 'Statistical Foundations of LLM-based A/B Testing: A Surrogacy Framework for Human Causal Inference' (2606.17165, 2026-06-15).
hot_topics.one_line: Researchers are asking language models to role-play survey respondents instead of paying real people, and statisticians are working out under what conditions, if any, the resulting numbers count as evidence about humans.
hot_topics.critic_note: Hot for about four years. 'Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples' is arXiv 2209.06899 (14 Sep 2022), the paper that put silicon sampling on the map, and 'Random Silicon Sampling: Simulating Human Sub-Population Opinion' is 2402.18144 (28 Feb 2024). The 2026 preprints are real (2607.03091 and 2606.13629 both appear in the arXiv listing), but the validity fight was already underway years earlier: 'How Many Human Survey Respondents is a Large Language Model Worth? An Uncertainty Quantification Perspective' is 2502.17773 (Feb 2025), and 'Not-quite-human tastes: the stylized omnivorousness of LLM survey surrogates' (2606.30085) sits in the same continuing stream. Venue evidence is also vague by the rubric: Metascience 2025 is a general conference whose themes merely include AI, not a dedicated session on this topic, and I did not fetch metascience.info to confirm the dates.

hot_topics.topic: Causal reasoning and causal discovery with foundation models
hot_topics.why_now: Causal discovery was historically bottlenecked on assumptions no dataset could supply. Foundation models put a large amount of encoded domain knowledge within reach as a prior over graph structure, which is either a genuine shortcut or a laundering of memorised text, and the field is currently arguing about which.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: CLeaR (Causal Learning and Reasoning) proceedings, PMLR volume 275 (CLeaR 2025) and volume 236 (CLeaR 2024), verified at proceedings.mlr.press. NeurIPS 2024 workshop 'Causality and Large Models', described as examining synergies between causal frameworks and foundation models (verified at neurips.cc/virtual/2024). NeurIPS 2025 workshop 'CauScien: Uncovering Causality in Science' (verified at neurips.cc/virtual/2025).
hot_topics.one_line: Trying to use a large model's absorbed world knowledge to propose which variables cause which, then testing whether that shortcut is real inference or just confident recall.

hot_topics.topic: Target trial emulation: forcing observational studies to declare a protocol first
hot_topics.why_now: Electronic health records, claims databases, and registries got large enough to answer treatment questions, and regulators began accepting real-world evidence. Target trial emulation is the discipline that stops those analyses from being retro-fitted, by making you write the randomised trial you wish you had run before you touch the data.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: Society for Causal Inference (sci-info.org), the organisation behind the American Causal Inference Conference, with its 2027 annual meeting announced (verified by fetch). Active 2026 methods work verified via alphaXiv: 'Improving Longitudinal Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation in Target Trial Emulation using Joint Calibrated Weights' (2606.04673, 2026-06-03) and 'A simple strategy for valid inference in target trial emulations' (2604.26471, 2026-04-29). Caveat: the per-year ACIC programme pages did not load for me, so I cannot name a target-trial-emulation-specific track or session with confidence.
hot_topics.one_line: Before analysing hospital records to ask whether a drug works, you first write down the exact clinical trial you would have run, then emulate it step by step, which blocks most of the ways observational studies fool themselves.

hot_topics.topic: High-dimensional asymptotics as the theory of scaling laws
hot_topics.subdomain: high-dimensional statistics and statistical learning theory
hot_topics.why_now: Training-budget decisions worth large amounts of compute currently rest on power-law curves fitted empirically with no theory behind the exponent. Random matrix theory and proportional asymptotics, the classical toolkit of high-dimensional statistics, turn out to predict those exponents, which makes compute allocation a statistics question.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: ICML 2026 workshop 'High Dimensional Learning Dynamics: the Science of Scaling', now in its fourth edition (the third edition ran at ICML 2025 as '3rd Workshop on High-dimensional Learning Dynamics'); its description targets 'rigorous mathematical frameworks connecting optimizer dynamics, architecture decisions, and data structure to observed power-law exponents' (both verified at icml.cc/virtual/2026 and icml.cc/virtual/2025). Contrast signal: 'High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems' (arXiv 2605.05076, 2026-05-06, via alphaXiv) is a retrospective, indicating the classical sparse-and-lasso regime is settled while the deep-learning-adjacent regime is not.
hot_topics.one_line: The old mathematics of 'more variables than data points' is being repurposed to explain why model performance improves as a specific power of compute, instead of that curve being an unexplained empirical fact.

hot_topics.topic: Amortized simulation-based inference with neural posterior estimation
hot_topics.why_now: Many scientific models are simulators you can run forward but whose likelihood you cannot write down. Neural density estimators let you train once on simulated data and then get a posterior for any new observation almost instantly, so the bottleneck moved from computation to diagnostics: detecting when the simulator is misspecified and whether the amortized posterior is actually calibrated.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: NeurIPS 2025 workshops 'Frontiers in Probabilistic Inference: Learning meets Sampling' and 'Structured Probabilistic Inference and Generative Modeling' (verified at neurips.cc/virtual/2025); SPIGM reappears as the '4th Structured Probabilistic Inference & Generative Modeling' workshop at ICML 2026 (verified at icml.cc/virtual/2026). 2026 work via alphaXiv: 'OASIS: Observation-Aware Simulation-Based Inference via Distributional Matching' (2606.22572, 2026-06-21), 'Amortized Simulation-Based Inference of Relativistic Mean-Field Couplings for Neutron-Star Equations of State' (2606.25446, 2026-06-24), 'Inverting Foundation Models of Brain Function with Simulation-Based Inference' (2604.23865, 2026-04-26). Caveat: I fetched simulation-based-inference.org and found a community resource hub but no dedicated standalone conference series, so the venue is ML-workshop-hosted rather than a symposium of its own.
hot_topics.one_line: When your scientific model is a simulator rather than an equation, you train a neural network once on many simulated runs so it can hand you a posterior for any real observation in milliseconds.

hot_topics.topic: Metascience becoming an institution: reproducibility infrastructure and AI inside the research pipeline
hot_topics.why_now: Replication moved from being a critique aimed at psychology to being funded infrastructure with its own alliance, funders, and policy audience, at exactly the moment generative AI started writing, reviewing, and analysing papers. That collision (automated production of plausible research at scale) is what makes 2025 and 2026 the inflection rather than 2015.
hot_topics.venue_evidence: Metascience 2025, University College London, 30 June to 2 July 2025, with named themes 'research assessment, funding, policymaking, artificial intelligence, open knowledge infrastructures, and responsible research practices', and the launch of the Metascience Alliance at that meeting. Series history verified at metascience.info/prior-conferences: 2019 Stanford, 2021 virtual, 2023 at the National Academy of Sciences in Washington DC, 2025 UCL. Metascience 2027 is announced for Montreal, 14 to 16 June 2027 (verified at metascience.info).
hot_topics.one_line: The study of how science itself works has grown from a critique into funded infrastructure with its own conference and alliance, and its current hardest problem is what happens when AI can generate plausible research faster than anyone can check it.
